topic: From Vibe Coding to Knowing What You Actually Wanted: Build a Requirement Ledger

key_points: Requirement drift is the most dangerous risk in vibe coding for long-running solo projects, worse than code quality or security holes
Both the model and the human forget: early goals get buried under debugging noise in the context window; vibe coding skips the thinking that fuzzy requirements used to force
Fix: put intent, constraints, and state into the repository so every new session can read them — CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, spec-driven work, PROGRESS.md/task logs, commit before stopping
AI cannot reconstruct original tradeoffs; it may rationalize the wrong direction and push drift deeper
Signs of drift: same issue fixed repeatedly, AI changes unrelated modules, can't explain why a directory exists, docs and behavior stop matching
Instructions become obsolete the moment code is generated — code becomes the only source of truth, and code is terrible at explaining why
Spec-driven development flips it: the spec is the authoritative blueprint the code must conform to; when something breaks you refine the spec and regenerate
Vibe coding still has a home at the unit/test level where scope is small enough to verify in isolation
Functionality flickering: unspecified details get filled in differently every generation (button blue one day, green the next)
Five anti-drift workflows: PRD.md (goals), GitHub Spec-Kit (spec/plan/tasks), Planning with Files (persist context), Ralph Wiggum Loop (autonomous), Superpowers (methodology library)
The Out of Scope section prevents scope creep before it happens
Treat each spec/plan/tasks artifact as a gate — review before proceeding, never /implement immediately
Worst mistake: generating artifacts and immediately implementing without reading them
Prompt drift: the slow slide away from the goal caused by vague instructions, long sessions, or lost context
Cure: a single-page 'current truth' document stating user, success criteria, non-negotiables — read it at the start of every session
Shorten cycles: one prompt, one change, one click-through; refresh the session and restate the plan
Best cure is a clear, testable outcome
72% of developers who tried AI coding tools use them every day
42% of their code is AI-generated/assisted (up from 6% in 2023), predicted to reach 65% by 2027
96% of developers don't fully trust AI-generated code is functionally correct; 61% say it looks correct but isn't reliable
67% of SMB devs report AI agents effective for vibe coding vs 52% at enterprises

stats.fact: Andrej Karpathy coined the term 'vibe coding' in February 2025; it was Collins Dictionary's Word of the Year for 2025.
92% of U.S. developers now cite using AI coding tools daily; AI generates ~41% of code worldwide.
Developers report 42% of their code is now AI-generated or assisted, up from 6% in 2023 and projected to reach 65% by 2027.
stats.source: Sonar State of Code Developer Survey (2026)

stats.fact: 96% of developers don't fully trust that AI-generated code is functionally correct; 61% agree AI often produces code that looks correct but isn't reliable.
stats.source: Sonar State of Code Developer Survey

stats.fact: In a 167-engineer survey, 17.5% opted out of AI code-editing tools entirely; the largest cohort (46.9%) said they were 'keeping up' with the trend.
A December 2025 study of open-source repositories found AI-generated code introduced security vulnerabilities in 45% of development tasks.
stats.source: IBM / academic study cited by IBM

stats.fact: As of late 2025, AI-generated code represents 22% of all merged code on GitHub, and ~46% of all written code was generated by Copilot.

angles: The real problem isn't bad code — it's losing the WHY: drift from original intent happens silently and compounds in long vibe-coding sessions
A 'requirement ledger' as the anti-drift primitive: the diff is the conversation, but your source of truth should be a versioned record of intent, decisions, and constraints in the repo
Both the model and the human forget — a ledger externalizes memory that neither a context window nor human recollection can hold reliably
Adapt ADR (Architecture Decision Record) practices from software architecture and apply them to vibe-coding prompts: intent, alternative ruled out, consequence
Spec-led regeneration beats patch-led repair: when something breaks, refine the spec and regenerate rather than whack-a-mole the code
